prompt: A bad desired-state commit triggers repeated failed reconciliation, a prune set includes shared state, and the Git source intermittently fails. Lead containment and recovery.
directAnswer: Declare deployment-control-plane and deletion risk; freeze promotion and stop retry amplification through the product's approved suspension/automation controls. Bind controller/source/application identities, failed commit and resolved artifact digests, render/policy results, retry/queue/API load, exact prune candidates with tracking/owners/finalizers/data policy, and Git authentication/availability. Preserve the failed revision and first resource error. Do not patch live while the bad source remains authoritative and do not approve prune. Revert to the last compatible desired revision or make a bounded forward fix, repair ownership/path so shared state is excluded, restore trusted source access, render/policy/diff again, then reconcile once. Verify controller conditions, inventory, rollout, dependencies, user SLI, no shared deletion, repository audit and removal of suspension/temporary credentials.
foundation: A bad source plus automatic retry and prune combines correctness, availability and data-loss hazards.
seniorAnswer: I protect retained state and the API from automation amplification first, then recover through an immutable reviewed source revision. I never manufacture Git truth from live output during an untrusted source outage.
weakAnswer: Disable GitOps, run kubectl apply from the last developer laptop, then re-enable prune.
whyWeak: It bypasses provenance/approval, creates ownership drift and can still delete shared state.

evidence.signal: failed revision plus first resource condition
evidence.proves: one desired revision failed at a boundary

evidence.signal: corrected revision, stable reconcile and user transaction

followUps.answer: Choose the smallest compatible desired-state change; data or migration compatibility can make forward fix safer.
Freeze promotion, preserve serving state, restore the trusted source/credential path, and reconcile the same known revision before new change.
Allow-empty guards, path/render tests, deletion review and stateful/shared ownership policy.
